title: Are bad reviews for Opening Night with Sheridan Smith justified?
transcript: If you are planning to go see Opening Night with Sheridan Smith, then think twice because those are three or four hours that you will never get back. Is it really bad as the reviews are suggesting? I thought that the only way to give a balanced opinion is to talk about positives, negatives, and some general thoughts about theater that this musical inspired me to have. So, to start with a few positives, I do think that Sheridan Smith is pretty good in this show. I have never seen her in anything else, so I have nothing to compare, and I'm not really familiar with her work. From my perspective, it really felt that this show was heavily on her shoulders, not only because she is the lead role, but I think apart from her and Nancy, which is a character that I'm going to talk about in a second, I don't really feel that anyone else contributed as much in terms of the character building and story arc. There are some sporadic characters that get involved every now and then, but it's very much show about Myrtle, who Sheridan is portraying, and that is kind of the glue that holds them all together. I'll talk a little bit more about storyline later, but now I do want to point out the second positive, and that is Shira Haas, who's playing the role of Nancy. And Nancy is this girl who got hit by a bus after she was greeted by Myrtle in front of the theater, that's Sheridan's character, and this has really made a profound impact on Myrtle, who was going through some personal issues, and she just kind of starts imagining Nancy coming back to her through all this process of them having previews on Broadway for the show that Myrtle is a star in. So, Shira, who plays Nancy, is really good at playing this really weird and a bit of a playful character, but at the same time, it is kind of a bit devilish. And I do think that some scenes between Myrtle and Nancy were really interesting in a sense that they really were a bit creepy, and it did feel like a turmoil of a person going through something. So, these two actors and these two characters have brought probably the most of interesting elements to the show. In particular, there was one when they are having a big fight, and this is obviously all happening in Myrtle's head, so it was really interesting way that they use cameras to delay, so you kind of can see like she's fighting on her own in this like big space, and it was just interesting the way that they have done it. I'd say that there are some interesting scenes in this musical, and one of those is also a scene between Myrtle and Morris, who are on stage partners in the play that they are putting on Broadway, but also they used to be married, so there's this whole complexity to their relationship. And in this scene, basically, they're just talking about life and how a lot of problems in life have answers, and one of the things that basically they do not have the answer to is kind of how to stop aging, which is something that Myrtle has an issue with throughout the whole show because she just refuses to portray this character that will typecast her as this kind of older woman or like neurotic woman. So, in this kind of very tender moment between the two of them, because the rest of the show is pretty much just tense between the two of them, they kind of exchange some really light-hearted conversations that are probably the most beautiful writing in the show. When it comes to positives, I have run out of them. I think the rest of the cast were decent, but this brings me to the negatives. So, I don't think that the cast has had a lot to work with in a sense that the story is very disjointed, and it doesn't really allow you to get yourself into it. A lot of these characters are just like scattered around and frantically trying to engage with Myrtle in most cases, and everything is just a bit messy, and I kind of left the theater feeling like, "What did I just watch, and why did I watch it? Like, what's the kind of overarching story?" It is one of those shows that puts that aging at the very center of the narrative and how women deal with aging. And personally, I'm just a little bit fed up with it. Like, I watched Sunset Boulevard, which had that as kind of the key theme as well, but I think Sunset Boulevard was a bit different because it talked about it through the prism of film noir and speaking movies and just generally kind of that feeling of time passing and you needing to adapt with the time, but I just feel that they tackled it in a completely different way. Whereas, like here, it's just like, "Oh, when you're a woman and you get to a certain age, like kind of like your life is over." This just felt like very plain and very boring from the storyline perspective. On a similar note, there are quite a few misogynistic types of sentences and lines and just generally portraying women as kind of these beings who are lonely and need to be loved, and if they are not loved, they just go mental. Even if that is something that you want to talk about or portray, there is a way to talk about it from the perspective of adding some value to the conversation or making people feel something. This is a musical, and you would think that at least there would be some catch tunes or something to hold onto. That's not the case. I did find that lack of depth also in the songs that are written for this musical, and I did not particularly enjoy any of them, quite frankly. And they also did not have really good lyrics to take you somewhere. And I also think that they were like jumping from like different styles. Sometimes it was more like Broadway, 42nd Street type of style, and sometimes it would be like more poppy. It just did not belong anywhere. That's kind of how I felt about it. My main issue with this musical is that it lacks substance, it lacks good story, and it lacks something that will change within you when you watch it. And, you know, you go to theater to experience something to change maybe your view a little bit on something or like introduce you to something slightly different. So, I did not really feel like that. I said at the beginning of the video that there is something just like generally in terms of the theater to talk about, and that is In this musical, there is a lot of camera work. So, the story is not only about putting this show on Broadway, but there's also like a documentary crew who is like filming all of this. And this documentary crew is all the time on stage, and there is a screen in the middle of the stage, and then if you're kind of sitting at the back, you have like a little television where you can also like see what's on that screen. And there are a lot of close-ups, a lot of interesting moments that are happening with this, but this is the fourth play that I've seen in the past year that really heavily relies on camera work. And I do appreciate innovation, and I think the way that Jamie Lloyd did it for Sunset Boulevard, it was really interesting because it is about film noir, and it is about the transition into the speaking movies, and for that purpose, it was really interesting to see how that could be used to really bring the story to life. I've also seen Oklahoma, which was doing this from a slightly different perspective, but lot of camera work, but also they had like quite a lot of scenes without it. And then, Dorian Gray is another play that I've seen, which really, really heavily relies on the camera work. It is essential for the way that the play is delivered. So, are we moving to something that is more cinematic theater and cinematography within the theater? I think it is an interesting avenue to explore, but do we need it in the theater, and to what degree? Just a bit bored of just close-ups and cameras and people on stage are filming, you know, the key actors and things like that. Maybe it's time to take a break from it. I am sad that I did not like this musical. I love going to the West End and seeing shows, so I would prefer that I went and I loved it, but there are plenty of other shows that I loved, and they are in this video here, and some of them have got some Olivier Awards as well, so please do check this video out if you want some more inspiration.
